description:
FamilySearch tree person read for Cornelius Driscoll (GJ72-9WD) WITH source descriptions, for the source-evaluation skill. Seven attached sources cover the three situations the shipped Hole corpus does not. DRIS-001 (Catholic parish baptism, with images) states 12 March 1814 at Skibbereen against the profile's '1814, Ireland' - a difference in PRECISION, not in value: the precise date falls inside the vague one, so the source refines the conclusion rather than contradicting it. DRIS-002 (Drouin marriage register, with images) indexes the marriage as 9 June 1845 against the profile's 9 June 1849 - same day, same month, same bride, same parish, one digit out on a record whose date is exact, so it is this corpus's genuine index error and the source `index_error_source` protects (as the substring "Drouin Collection", which no other source here shares). DRIS-003 (Catholic parish burial) and DRIS-004 (Quebec civil death registration) both bear on a death the profile does NOT record, and they disagree with each other by seven years - buried 14 April 1878 against died 2 February 1885. Both carry an indexed birth of 1814, so neither is the wrong man; that indexed birth is how this corpus expresses a stated age at death, since no fixture in the repo uses an Age fact type. DRIS-005 (1851 census, index only) disagrees on ONE field, the township, and carries no birth year, no household and no spouse, so it is genuinely undecidable between a place keyed to the wrong jurisdiction and a same-name man in the next township - the ambiguous case that must not be collapsed. DRIS-006 (1861 census) indexes a birth of 1816, about two years off the baptism's 1814: ordinary census variance, and a deliberate NON-finding both against the profile and as a source-vs-source pair. SD-DRIS-F is a contributor upload with no record ARK and must be reported unchecked rather than clean. Internal ids (P1/N1/F1/S1) recur across the record fixtures exactly as they do in the Hole corpus, because that is how the tool numbers them. Scenario: driscoll-source-audit.

Predicate is `personId` ALONE. `sourceDescriptions` and `relatives` are accepted and IGNORED by the tool since #2666 — its schema says so — so a model that omits them is reading the tool correctly, and a predicate demanding one makes the fixture miss and the whole run collapse into fixture_not_found. Measured 2026-10-01: every call in that run sent `{personId}` alone, 9 of 11 tests failed, and the earlier runs were already mixed (some calls with, some without) — brittle before, broken after.
